title: Merrick and Massapequa: A Local Account of Refuge
summary: A Baldwin local history remembers Massapequa people offering refuge to Merrick families displaced by colonial settlement.
address_label: Regional Merrick–Massapequa history; no identified parcel
ancestral_territory_note: Linked to Merrick Ancestral Land with recognition of overlapping Merikoke/Merrick and Massapequa histories.
why_this_matters: Displacement also brought people into relationships of refuge and support. This local account remembers connections between neighboring Native communities during colonial expansion.
introduction_title: Refuge in a Later Local History
introduction_content:
Baldwin: Our Heritage, published in 1976, describes Massapequa people offering refuge to Merrick families displaced by colonial settlement in Kings County. The account places Merrick or Merikoke homes between Parsonage Creek and Fort Neck Creek.

This remembered relationship places the history of refuge and mutual support alongside the history of land loss.
whereintheworld_content: The account belongs to the intertwined histories of Merrick and Massapequa on Long Island’s South Shore.

source_list.title: Baldwin: Our Heritage, 1976
source_list.citation_context: Baldwin: Our Heritage (1976), p.3. Attributed later account of refuge; no surveyed shared-land parcel.
